| Country | Population Growth % | Birth Rate /1 000 | Life Expectancy (years) |
|---------|---------------------|-------------------|--------------------------|
| Canada | 0.170 % | 10.28 / 1 000 | 81.23 y |
| France | 0.549 % | 12.57 / 1 000 | 80.98 y |
| Australia | 1.195 % | 12.47 / 1 000 | 81.63 y |

*Sources: University of Toronto G7 Information Center – “G8 and G20 Demographics” fact sheet (2010).*  
(See table excerpts: Canada 0.170 %, 10.28 /1 000, 81.23 y; France 0.549 %, 12.57 /1 000, 80.98 y; Australia 1.195 %, 12.47 /1 000, 81.63 y – https://g7.utoronto.ca/evaluations/factsheet/factsheet_demography.html.)

**Unemployment‑rate evidence**  
The “G8 and G20 Economic Indicators” fact sheet (2010) lists “Unemployment Rate 2009” values, but the figures appear as negative or anomalous numbers (e.g., Canada “–36.13 %”, France “–38.84 %”), suggesting the data are not reliable unemployment statistics. Consequently, the 2009 unemployment rate (< 9.50 %) for Canada, France, and Australia cannot be confirmed from these sources.

**Conclusion**  
Only Canada, France, and Australia satisfy the demographic thresholds (positive population growth, birth rate > 10, life expectancy > 80). Whether each country’s 2009 unemployment rate fell below 9.50 % is unverified with the available University of Toronto fact sheets. No other G20 member country meets all four conditions.
